scope: Research and code-path review only. No engine, questionbank, model responses or live site edited. Supplied catalog is public; no private model files accessed.
mainConclusion: Broaden discovery and catalog coverage, but differentiate the actual work before confirmation. Doctor, lawyer and five engineering occupations already exist; their low frequency must be diagnosed as evidence, exposure, ranking/display, route or missing-specialty issues separately. Broad interest types and repeated generic options cannot substitute for domain-specific inquiry.

sources.title: O*NET Interest Profiler Manual, March 2021
sources.evidence: The validated Interest Profiler measures six RIASEC interests. Its Short Form has60items and Mini-IP30. Reliability, validity, occupational linkage and interpretation are documented separately. These findings do not validate Fieldguide’s editorial follow-ups or its matching thresholds.

sources.title: O*NET Content Model
sources.evidence: Separates worker interests, abilities, knowledge and education from job tasks, activities and work context, and from market information. Activities form general, intermediate and detailed levels.

sources.title: O*NET May2026 Specific Interest information release
sources.evidence: May2026 introduced41specific-interest areas with occupational profiles for891data-level occupations, populated using a hybrid artificial intelligence-expert method. Treat occupational descriptors as occupational data, not student norms or a validated new Fieldguide assessment.

sources.title: Updating Vocational Interests Information for the O*NET Content Model
sources.evidence: Defines41basic-interest areas based on CABIN, with activity and occupation examples. Describes interest items as actions tied to objects/context. Medical Science, Health Care Service, Engineering and Law distinguish domains that broad helping or problem-solving can conflate.

sources.title: Su etal.,2019. Toward a dimensional model of vocational interests
sources.evidence: Develops41homogeneous basic-interest scales and an8dimension SETPOINT hierarchy. Working-adult structural and occupational-membership evidence supports measuring activity preferences below broad interest dimensions; it does not establish Fieldguide adolescent cutoffs.

sources.title: Chu etal. Interest Fit Beyond the RIASEC: CABIN-NET
sources.evidence: A60item measure of20basic-interest scales was developed in768adults and studied longitudinally in816four-year university and560community-college graduates. Authors report stronger career-outcome prediction from basic-interest fit than RIASEC fit. Transfer to younger students or our custom branching requires validation.
sources.licensingNote: Repository manuscript license is CC BY-NC-ND4.0. Do not assume unrestricted reuse/adaptation of instrument items; verify separate instrument permission. Proposed items below are original editorial drafts.

sources.title: Nye etal.,2012. Vocational Interests and Performance
sources.evidence: Across60studies and approximately568correlations, interests related to performance/persistence and person-environment congruence was more predictive than interest scores alone. Association is neither guaranteed career success nor a precise individual probability.

sources.title: Hoff etal. Adolescent vocational interests predict early career success: Two12-year longitudinal studies
sources.evidence: Two12-year samples of485and1290participants followed interests from late adolescence. Better eventual vocational fit related to later job satisfaction; interest levels and change were studied as separate predictors. This supports revisiting exploration rather than treating one profile as permanent.

sources.title: Alkan and Deniz,2023. Developing a Computerized Adaptive Test Form of the Occupational Field Interest Inventory
sources.evidence: Post-hoc CAT simulations on1425high-school students averaged59items, with correlations.91–.97between paper scores and simulated theta estimates. Efficiency depended on a calibrated item bank, model and stopping rules. It does not validate an arbitrary short decision tree.

sources.title: Kirkendall etal. Adaptive vocational interest diagnostic: Informing and improving the job assignment process
sources.evidence: Describes a military instrument combining broad/narrow interests, adaptive testing and forced choice. Useful precedent for a hierarchical architecture; civilian adolescent transfer, fake resistance and efficiency are not established for Fieldguide.

sources.title: 2024 NCDA Code of Ethics
sources.evidence: SectionsE.1–E.3require appropriate use, explanation and sound interpretation. E.6recommends considering validity/reliability/limitations and multiple evidence forms. E.8requires caution about population/context differences. E.9requires qualification of results from insufficiently supported instruments; E.10addresses assessment permission.
sources.verification: Official PDF downloaded and text extracted locally; web parser returned an error.

sources.title: O*NET Scales, Ratings, and Standardized Scores
sources.evidence: O*NET calls a task core when relevance is at least67percent and mean importance at least3.0. This does not mean every individual performs every core task, or that every task should be a mandatory student-interest gate.

sources.title: O*NET29-1215.00 Family Medicine Physicians
sources.evidence: Tasks include diagnosis using history/tests, choosing treatment, monitoring progress and communicating with patients; family medicine is one physician occupation, not all physician specialties.

sources.title: O*NET23-1011.00 Lawyers
sources.evidence: Tasks span legal interpretation/research, evidence, advising clients, drafting/reviewing documents, negotiation and representation. Courtroom argument alone does not cover the occupation.

sources.title: O*NET17-2141.00 Mechanical Engineers
sources.evidence: Tasks span mechanical design, drawings, evaluation/testing, technical constraints and system modification. Device interest needs differentiation from maintenance and from other engineering domains.

sources.title: O*NET19-1042.00 Medical Scientists, Except Epidemiologists
sources.evidence: Tasks include designing studies of disease/treatment, evaluating biological effects, analyzing samples/data and communicating research findings. Clinical diagnosis and direct patient care are not interchangeable with research interest.

sources.title: O*NET15-2031.00 Operations Research Analysts
sources.evidence: Describes mathematical modeling, optimization and analysis to improve decisions. It offers a quantitative decision-science branch distinct from engineering physical objects and generic project coordination.

actualCodeGatesAndRisks.observation: No comparison invitations for incomplete, flat or near-flat profiles. Entry requires eligible whole-profile fit plus an opportunity or focused-field like; alternate opportunity route requiresr>=.2andtaskEvidence>=3. All-connected-field conflict and role/route conflict also suppress invitations.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.risk: Plausible narrow interests can remain unasked when a broad profile is weak or field questions do not represent them. This is a code-path risk, not proof that this caused any specific zero count.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.proposal: Allow an explicitly labeled student-selected discovery path from search or a domain probe even with incomplete/flat profiles. Keep Top evidence standards separate and explain why results are provisional.

actualCodeGatesAndRisks.observation: First3invitations are immediately visible; remaining options are inside More professions to compare.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.risk: Visibility and eligible-candidate availability differ. A zero in displayed match counts can reflect ordering/caps rather than career ineligibility.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.proposal: Record eligible/invited/visible/started/completed separately; expose domain-diverse exploration and user search.

actualCodeGatesAndRisks.observation: Field support uses mean correlation of3leading catalog occupations, threshold.608, plus focused-field confirmation and fewer than2concerns. Suggested fields are capped3.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.risk: The field score depends on current catalog composition; adding careers can change field exposure before any new student answer.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.proposal: Freeze/version field vectors or explicitly audit expansion effects on old fields. Offer all fields through exploration navigation.

actualCodeGatesAndRisks.observation: Direct support requires3nonroute question groups and2derived domains plus whole-profile fit or a6group repeated-task alternative. The alternative further needs3refinement groups and4focused groups; counting depends on selected options.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.risk: Repeated variants of the same activity can look like independent evidence, while a profession omitted from mapped options cannot gather enough evidence.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.proposal: Represent activity/domain/outcome evidence explicitly. Count semantically distinct constructs, not question IDs alone; give each new profession balanced positive, adjacent and contradiction probes.

actualCodeGatesAndRisks.observation: Evidence domain is inferred from question ID substrings. One family with most matching nonroute questions is selected;4questions chosen for specificity/domain coverage.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.risk: Naming conventions can create artificial independence. Cross-field professions are reduced to one family; more catalog entries can increase repeated shared options without useful differentiation.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.proposal: Add explicit domain/construct/role-family/question-purpose metadata and source mappings. Reuse relevant cross-field responses and branch to the missing differentiator.

actualCodeGatesAndRisks.observation: Clinical-role checks distinguish7medical/dental roles. Physician, NP and PA share many broad items, then role names and preparation routes separate them. health focusedRoles excludes other roles when a focused role has been selected.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.risk: A novice can understand symptom investigation yet not know PA/NP/physician responsibilities or route terminology. More specifically, roleFocusElsewhere applies to every health-family occupation once any focused clinical role is selected, so a clinical choice can exclude nonclinical health ideas such as epidemiology in that family. This is an actual gate; its contribution to observed model counts still needs a controlled replay.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.proposal: Provide neutral role explanations and work scenarios before named-role choices; support multiple interests. Keep actual prescribing scope, training and licensure accurate and separate from interest.

actualCodeGatesAndRisks.observation: Mechanical, electrical and biomedical engineering share many identical options; biomedical is linked to generic devices/circuits before its2defining medical-device questions. Catalog contains5engineering occupations.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.risk: Question count overstates breadth; repeated generic device evidence cannot decide a medical-device interest or reveal omitted chemical/environmental/computer/aerospace areas.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.proposal: Probe design object and problem domain before specialization; map a given domain to engineer, technician, researcher and trade alternatives with differentiated work activities.

actualCodeGatesAndRisks.observation: Current0.44requires2defining Yes responses. Direct responses support confirmation; inferred responses support only high/medium confidence. ExplicitNo declines; unsure/unfamiliar stays pending.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.risk: Improved content avoids the former unfamiliar-tools gate, but2Yes is an editorial rule, not a validated standard. Leading or compound prompts can still inflate endorsement.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.proposal: Keep provenance and unresolvedness visible; test single-concept wording, contradictions and alternate second probes. Never treat inferred answers as real student choices.

actualCodeGatesAndRisks.observation: Among similar relevance candidates, education preference and lifestyle coverage affect invitation ordering. A relevant degree option is inserted if willing/open to college or graduate study and the initial3have none.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.risk: This helps exposure but cannot establish suitability. Pay and education routing can change which questions are answered before outcomes are calculated.
actualCodeGatesAndRisks.proposal: Measure exposure stratified by route and interest strength. Keep salary, prestige, education preference and affordability outside interest evidence.

questionArchitectureProposal.status: Original design proposal informed by sources; unvalidated until tested with students and independent expert review.

layers.detail: Preserve licensed O*NET instrument wording, administration and scoring. Store editorial domain/role probes separately; do not call their results O*NET scores or aptitude measures.

Use the41O*NET specific-interest areas as an occupational coverage checklist and a mapping aid. Introduce concrete activity probes for omitted areas such as medical research, law, engineering domains, mathematical optimization, finance and research. Use broad scores to prioritize, not permanently exclude.

Let students search any profession or select a domain. Ask what is attractive about it; a title choice starts exploration, it does not become a Top match. Allow uncertain/flat profiles to learn about work without pretending precision.

Ask about two distinct defining activities and at least one adjacent-role contrast. Use examples that do not require already knowing professional software, jargon, admissions rules or job titles. A learner should be able to imagine the activity.

Select a follow-up about the largest missing distinction, not another paraphrase of the same interest. Explain unfamiliar work neutrally, then let the student answer; keep before/after responses and whether information was shown.

After interest evidence, show training paths, licensing, academic preparation and supports, costs, time and staged pay. Distinguish interest, willingness to pursue a route and current eligibility. Keep first-paid-stage lifestyle checks and residency/prior-experience treatment.

responseDesign.interest: Five ordered anchors from strongly dislike to strongly like, with neutral/unsure; provide separate I do not yet understand this activity. Prototype choice, not validated scale.
responseDesign.exposure: Optional separate Have tried / Have observed / Have only heard of it / New to me; do not give extra interest credit for costly prior exposure.
responseDesign.selfEfficacy: Optional Can imagine learning this with support / Unsure / Want to discuss barriers. Do not mix confidence, current skill or school access into interest.
responseDesign.pairedComparisons: Use occasional adjacent-role contrasts with both/neither/unsure options; do not force students into one domain. Randomize option order in evaluation.

burdenProposal.initialDomainProbes: Prototype 8–12 short activity probes selected across underrepresented domains after the existing broad inventory, with a browse-all alternative.
burdenProposal.focusedBranch: Prototype 3–5 new questions per chosen branch, reuse genuine prior evidence, typically explore 2–3 branches and allow save/resume.
burdenProposal.qualification: These are product targets to test for completion, comprehension, accessibility and recall. They are not a psychometric minimum or a validated adaptive stopping rule. Do not call rule-based branching calibrated CAT.

branchingExamples.catalogStatus: Already present as physician; not absent from catalog. Expand physician specialties only after distinguishing them.
branchingExamples.trigger: Interest in disease mechanisms plus patient-facing diagnosis, or explicit medical exploration; generic helping alone is insufficient.

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy learning to compare a patient’s symptoms, health history and test results to work out what may be causing an illness?
Would you enjoy learning to choose a medical treatment with a patient and check over time whether it is helping?

Which work would you like to investigate further: diagnosing and treating an individual patient; studying disease in a research project; tracking illness across a community; or supporting daily patient care? Choose any, or unsure.
Imagine two illnesses could explain the same symptoms. Would comparing the evidence and explaining why one diagnosis fits better hold your interest?
After learning about this work, would you like to compare medical school and residency with other health-care preparation routes?

branchingExamples.branching: Patient diagnosis+treatment opens physician/PA/NP work comparisons with neutral scope/role descriptions; research opens medical scientist; community patterns opens epidemiology. Definite dislike of direct clinical work should not imply dislike of medical science. No automatic physician promotion from two generic helping answers.

branchingExamples.catalogStatus: Already present as law; title law may obscure that this includes lawyers.
branchingExamples.trigger: Interest in rights/rules plus using evidence or careful language to advise/represent others. Being argumentative, sociable or interested in fairness alone is insufficient.

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy learning to read laws and earlier legal decisions to explain how they apply to someone’s situation?
Would you enjoy learning to build a well-supported legal recommendation after comparing facts and opposing arguments?

Which legal activities would you like to try learning: advising a client; drafting a contract; negotiating a dispute; presenting an argument in court; or organizing evidence for a legal team? Choose any, or unsure.
If a case has a sympathetic person but mixed evidence, would you want to investigate the facts and explain the limits of their legal position?
How do you feel about work that involves substantial reading, precise writing and deadlines?

branchingExamples.branching: Core legal analysis+advice can support law exploration even if courtroom performance is unattractive; legal-team evidence work opens paralegal; general policy/justice interest opens public policy/social research. Do not make criminal defense, litigation or enjoying public speaking mandatory for all lawyers.

branchingExamples.catalogStatus: 5 current occupations: mechanical, civil, electrical, biomedical and industrial engineering. Engineer should be a discovery family, not one undifferentiated match.
branchingExamples.trigger: Interest in designing/test-improving systems under real constraints, or explicit domain exploration; liking mathematics or assembling things alone is insufficient.

questions.prompt: Which problems would you like to learn to design solutions for: machines and motion; electricity and electronics; buildings and water systems; materials and chemical processes; aircraft and spacecraft; computer hardware; medical devices; or production systems? Choose any, or unsure.
Would you enjoy learning to compare design options using calculations and tests before deciding which solution is likely to work?
Would you enjoy revising a design when tests show a weakness, while balancing safety, cost and how people will use it?
Would you rather explore designing a new system, building/installing it, maintaining and repairing it, or investigating the science behind it? Choose any, or unsure.

For medical devices: would designing equipment used to diagnose or treat health conditions interest you, even when much of the work is testing and documenting rather than caring directly for patients?

branchingExamples.branching: Domain selection opens matching engineer/technician/scientist/trade activities. Preserve overlap without treating interest in generic gadgets as biomedical interest. Environmental/chemical/computer/aerospace branches require their own sourced questions and route/pay data before live matching.

branchingExamples.catalogStatus: Not present under this occupation/SOC in supplied117career catalog.
branchingExamples.trigger: Interest in biology/disease and experimental investigation; can emerge from science or health, including dislike of patient care.

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy learning to design a study that tests a possible explanation for how a disease develops or how a treatment works?
Would you enjoy learning to analyze biological samples or research results and explain what they do and do not show?
Would you prefer to investigate disease in a research study, diagnose individual patients, or study health patterns in whole communities? Choose any, or unsure.
Would repeating a careful procedure and checking unexpected results appeal to you, or would you want to learn more about that routine first?

branchingExamples.branching: Research/design interest opens medical scientist; reliable-lab-procedure interest may also open biological technician or clinical laboratory scientist; patient diagnosis routes toward clinical roles; population patterns routes toward epidemiology. Do not require intent to practice medicine.

branchingExamples.catalogStatus: Not present under this occupation/SOC in supplied117career catalog.
branchingExamples.trigger: Interest in quantitative decision-making under constraints; can connect data, logistics, public-service or engineering interests.

questions.prompt: Would you enjoy learning to build a mathematical model that compares ways to use limited staff, time or resources?
Would you enjoy testing how a recommended plan changes when demand, costs or assumptions change?
Would you like to explore optimizing a decision with a model, finding patterns in data, coordinating an agreed project, or designing physical equipment? Choose any, or unsure.
Would explaining a model’s assumptions and limitations to people making a decision interest you?

branchingExamples.branching: Optimization under constraints opens operations research; pattern-finding opens data science/statistics; coordination opens project/logistics roles. Spreadsheet familiarity or enjoyment of gaming strategy alone does not establish the profession.

scoringAndInterpretationProposal.status: Proposed evidence model, not empirical validated thresholds or likelihoods.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.independentEvidence: Track broad fit, domain interest, at least two semantically distinct defining-activity endorsements, adjacent-role differentiation, explicit contradictions and route/context information separately. Do not count the same answer multiple times because it appears in several fields or supports several occupations.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.discovery: Use weaker evidence to ask a question or offer a low-stakes work sample. Exposure eligibility should be wider than confirmed match eligibility.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.top: Require coherent occupation-specific evidence without unresolved defining-work contradictions. Compare similarly supported careers; show ties and why. Do not convert more total questions, a degree label or higher pay into stronger interest.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.negative: A clear dislike of a defining activity counts against that occupation. A dislike of an optional task, specialty or setting should branch to other variants rather than reject the whole profession. Check comprehension before treating a novice response as a firm conflict.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.unknown: Unfamiliar/unsure is missing information, not zero interest and not implicit Yes. Offer a neutral description or safe sample and ask again. Preserve status until resolved; do not impute hidden preferences from biography or demographics.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.provenance: Separate actual student choices from profile-inferred simulation answers. Inference confidence is not a psychometric probability. Show evidence excerpts and unresolved questions; original frozen histories stay immutable.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.interestVersusFeasibility: Interest evidence may justify a profession even when training feasibility is unresolved or entry pay does not sustain the lifestyle. State each separately. Financial feasibility must not create interest evidence; high salary must not be used as a rescue match.
scoringAndInterpretationProposal.unvalidatedRules: Use transparent provisional rule thresholds initially and prospectively evaluate them. A copiedO*NETcorrelation threshold or twoYesrule does not acquire validity from using occupational source data.

fairnessAndLimits: Equal opportunity to learn about unfamiliar work is different from assigning equal numbers of professions. Do not use gender, ethnicity, family income or school prestige as an interest shortcut.

An adolescent without shadowing or lab access can express a coherent learning interest; lack of expensive exposure is not a disqualifier. Conversely, family exposure or a prestigious title is not sufficient evidence.
Current skill, grade history, self-efficacy, disability and financial/training barriers should be discussed as supports or feasibility, not silently treated as dislike.

RIASEC and basic-interest validity evidence is population- and instrument-specific. Fieldguide editorial questions remain exploration tools until their own validation; source-linked task accuracy alone is insufficient.

Published adult/graduate observational findings do not establish causal benefits of the proposed interface. Simulation/biography agreement tests consistency and code behavior, not student-outcome validity.

evaluationPlan.actions: Create occupation×domain×activity×route coverage matrix, mapped to SOCs and current source versions. Identify missing questions before model replays. Independent occupational experts review defining versus optional tasks and adjacent-role distinctions.

Cognitive interviews with diverse secondary students, including limited work exposure, different language backgrounds, disability/access needs and rural/low-resource contexts. Ask students to explain prompts in their own words; track jargon, leading wording and reading burden.

Keep 0.41, 0.42 and 0.44 answers and chart outputs frozen. Freeze the new question bank and offered manifest before biography-only authors answer new items. Authors must not see desired careers, outcomes or engine gates. Compare old/new status with explicit reason codes and evidence; never tune to make every model receive a degree profession.

Retain unseen holdout profiles and add counterexamples: generic helping without diagnosis; science curiosity without patient care; justice concern without legal reasoning; gadgets without medical devices; mathematics without optimization; writing without law; strong interest with low prior exposure; and clear No despite a high salary target. Check false promotions and missed plausible invitations.

Prospectively measure comprehension, completion, question burden, stability, response distributions and whether students recognize the offered work. Use independent counselor judgments and subsequent voluntary work-sample reactions as limited criteria, not agreement with the engine itself. If using a new scored scale, evaluate reliability, dimensionality, external validity and calibration before claiming a validated assessment.

Audit invited, visible, started, completed, eligible, Top, Other, pending and sustaining separately by field/route and available consented subgroup variables. Test differential item functioning/measurement comparability only with adequate data; do not infer sensitive traits from names. Evaluate whether unfamiliar responses concentrate in groups with less exposure. No numerical parity targets that force unsuitable matches.

Report unique model counts and capped visible-list counts separately, ties, evidence insufficiency and catalog absence. Track questions asked per supported offer, breadth of interest coverage, false promotion rate, missed-domain invitations and unresolved status. A higher degree Top count alone is not success.

implementationOrderProposal: Publish this audit with catalog and exposure distinctions.
Add transparent browse/search and domain discovery probes for existing overlooked professions, without changing Top thresholds automatically.
Prioritize new degree occupations by missing domains and independent source coverage, then author distinct activity questions and neutral role explanations.
Complete route/licensing/cost/first-paid-stage pay data for every new occupation before offering lifestyle coverage.
Freeze new questions, author unseen profile-consistent answers, run holdout evaluation and publish stage-by-stage chart differences with reasons.
Pilot with actual students before claiming scoring validity or calibrated adaptive efficiency.
